'''''Star Wars: The Rebel Files''''', officially named as '''''The Rebel Files: Collected Intelligence of the Alliance''''' is a reference book written by [[Daniel Wallace]]. The book, similar to [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] titles such as [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path'']], contains in-universe and documents about the procedures, equipment and personnel of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]]. The boxed set was released on [[November 21]], [[2017]]. A book-only edition was later released on [[July 3]], [[2018]].

==Publisher's summary==
''This top-secret cache reproduces highly sensitive intelligence that traces the Rebel Alliance from its formation through its tireless fight against the Empire. From its earliest beginnings in covert opposition to Imperial operations, the Alliance could not trust its most sensitive information to risk of digital interception. Instead, it was kept in a secure case, traveling with key senior Rebel personnel. Lost in the chaos surrounding the Battle of Endor, it was rediscovered many years later by the newly formed Resistance''.

''Richly illustrated and full of strategic detail and history, the files also feature additional annotation by Resistance members such as General Leia Organa, Mon Mothma, Poe Dameron, and Admiral Ackbar, making this a crucial read for fans seeking a deeper understanding of the saga.''

==Development==
It was first to be released in [[October]] [[2017]].<ref name="EW">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/comic-con/star-wars-the-last-jedi-book-series-covers|text=Here Are All The ''Star Wars'' Covers in ''The Last Jedi'' Book Series|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2017-07-20|archiveurl=https://archive.is/NoxWC}}</ref>

According to a [[StarWars.com]] blog entry dated [[October 7]], 2017, the deluxe edition of ''Star Wars: The Rebel Files'' was scheduled to be released in the United States on [[November 14]] of that year,<ref name="NYCC 2017">{{SW|url=news/nycc-2017-artist-joe-corroney-on-the-upcoming-star-wars-rebel-files-book|text=NYCC 2017: Artist Joe Corroney On The Upcoming ''Star Wars: Rebel Files'' Book}}</ref> but no such product was available. Major online book retailers [[Wikipedia:Amazon (company)|Amazon]] and [[Wikipedia:Barnes & Noble|Barnes & Noble]] didn't have a product listing for the deluxe edition. Only Australian online retailers indicated that the deluxe edition would be released in Australia on [[December 1]], 2017.<ref name="Booktopia" /><ref name="Dymocks" /> The deluxe edition started to appear on online retailers on [[November 19]].

==Continuity==
*On page 14, [[Hera Syndulla]] is referred to as Spectre One, when that [[callsign]] was attributed to [[Kanan Jarrus]] in ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''.
*Page 15 has a photo of the [[Spectres]] after the [[Mission to Malachor]]. This is inconsistent, as the photo was being used by [[Ahsoka Tano]] in a document demonstrating the Spectres to [[Rebel Alliance Intelligence Service]]. Ahsoka had no contact with the Spectres during the time portrayed in the photo. Additionally, the photo depicts the Spectres as they appeared during [[Star Wars Rebels Season Three|Season Three]] of ''Star Wars Rebels'', rather than [[Star Wars Rebels Season Two|Season Two]], when the mission took place.
*On page 17, [[Jun Sato]]'s surname is misspelled "Soto."
*On page 18, in a letter to [[Moff]] [[Stattata]], [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] states that she arrived on [[Lothal]] at the [[capital]]; she actually arrived at [[Jalath]].
*On page 25, an image of the [[Thranta-class corvette|''Thranta''-class corvette]] from the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] video game ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' was used in place of the [[canon]] [[Sphyrna-class Hammerhead corvette|''Sphyrna''-class Hammerhead corvette]].
*On page 38, the map of [[the galaxy]] mistakenly depicts [[Alderaan]] as being in the [[Colonies]] instead of the [[Core Worlds]] and has the labels for the [[Expansion Region]] and the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]] improperly switched.
*On page 122, [[Amilyn Holdo]] states that the [[Resistance]] did not have any [[Spy|spies]] within the [[First Order]]. However, ''[[Poe Dameron: Flight Log]]'' previously established that the [[Resistance spy droid network]] did have spies, including [[RA-7-D4]], within the First Order.<ref name="Flight Log">''[[Poe Dameron: Flight Log]]''</ref>
*On page 145, Lothal is included as part of a list of highlighted targets for [[Operation Ringbreaker]]. However, the ''Star Wars Rebels'' [[Star Wars Rebels Season Four|Season Four]] episodes "[[Family Reunion – and Farewell]]" would later reveal that Lothal was liberated from Imperial rule years before the operation and would stay that way past the events of the [[Battle of Endor]], thus leaving its inclusion in the highlighted targets to be contradictory.
*On page 146, [[Sullust]] is misspelled "Sollust" at one point.
*On page 152, the image of the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]]'s [[reactor]] core is upside-down.
*On page 153, [[Basteel]], [[Jaresh]] and [[Sesid]] are all misspelled as "Bastille," "Juresh" and "Sessid".
*On page 160, [[hyperdrive]] is misspelled as "hyerdrive".
*On page 165, [[Haxen Delto]]'s name is misspelled as "Haxan".
*On page 166, [[Poe Dameron]] states that prior to the [[Battle of Endor]], his [[Parent|mother]], [[Shara Bey]], would have been prepping her [[X-wing starfighter]], when she [[pilot]]s an [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]].
*Originally, [[Davits Draven]] was alive until at least during the [[rescue of Han Solo]] and just prior to the Battle of Endor in [[4 ABY]] as ''Star Wars: The Rebel Files'' had established. Due to a miscommunication, notes were missed during production of ''Star Wars: The Rebel Files''. [[Star Wars (2015) 54|''Star Wars'' (2015) 54]] had Draven dying aboard the ''Executor''. [[Matt Martin]] specified that for the time being, the comic is the definitive story for Draven.<ref name="Tweet 1">{{Twitter|missingwords|status/1042535819339161600|[[Matt Martin]]|quote=Yeah, we're aware. It sounds like there were some notes missed somewhere down the production pipeline. We're hoping to have it fixed in future printings of the book. For now, you can assume that the comic is the definitive story for that character.|archivedate=20200814213543}}</ref><ref name="Tweet 2">{{Twitter|missingwords|status/1042824623941771264|[[Matt Martin]]|quote=That death was plotted for Marvel before Rebel Files was written. Remember, the order things come out isn't necessarily the order they're created. A note was given in the RF manuscript to remove the mentions of that character after a certain time but fell through the cracks.|archivedate=20200813210814}}</ref>
*In a similar situation to Davits Draven, [[Jan Dodonna]] is stated to be alive post-Hoth despite his death in [[Star Wars (2015) 55|''Star Wars'' (2015) 55]]. Similarly, the comic book's timeline of events takes priority, and the contradiction is planned to be fixed in later reprints of ''Star Wars: The Rebel Files''.<ref name="Tweet 3">{{Twitter|missingwords|status/1047511438259052544|[[Matt Martin]]|quote=It's on the list.|archivefile=File:MattMartin-Death-October-3-2019.png}}</ref>
